intended_object: An additive equivalence between two presentations of the same quotient. One side is the symbol ring modulo the order initial ideal, seen as a k-submodule through `restrictScalars`. The other is the library's `OrderCharacteristicModule`. Both sides agree by definition. This reading comes from the docstring and the body.
explanation: The body is `Quotient.congr` applied to the identity equivalence, and every proof obligation closes by `rfl`. So the two quotients are definitionally the same type, and this declaration only transports between two ways of writing it, through `restrictScalars`, which changes the scalar ring of the ideal. It is a coercion or bookkeeping device that the library uses for its internal proofs. It has no mathematical content beyond the trivial identity of the underlying additive quotient, so it is an implementation detail, not a mathematical object.
